title: Black Bank Hassock
summary: Black Bank Hassock is the third of the grouped Hassock entries and is identified as another tract in the same East Rockaway Inlet locality as Great Bear Hassock.
address_label: East Rockaway Inlet, Queens/Nassau County, New York
map_geometry_source: Approximate general location based on Tooker identifying Black Bank Hassock as another meadow tract near East Rockaway Inlet; offset slightly for map visibility.
why_this_matters: Black Bank Hassock preserves a meadow-name near East Rockaway Inlet, with the Hassock element connected to grass, sedge, or marsh land. That meaning points to the importance of South Shore wetlands as places of material knowledge, where grasses and sedges could support mats, coverings, and daily work. Marshes are culturally meaningful Native landscapes, not empty or marginal ground.
history_content: Black Bank Hassock is preserved as a distinct meadow tract rather than a spelling variant. The exact tract has not yet been matched to a modern parcel or named landscape feature.
translation_content:
The Hassock names share a marsh-place explanation. Related language examples include Narragansett hassucki, meaning marsh land, and Delaware assisku, meaning miry or marshy. Rassapeague is a related marsh-place vocabulary entry and remains a separate site.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous place names are not merely location names. They have power. They speak stories.”

— Adam Keawe Manalo-Camp, What's in a Name? (2023), opening discussion
land_loss_content: Black Bank Hassock helps show how named marsh and meadow tracts structured the south-shore inlet landscape. Recording the name with a general marker preserves the place reference while keeping the exact location open for future map and deed review.
whereintheworld_content: The point shown is an approximate general marker near East Rockaway Inlet. It is offset slightly from the nearby Great Bear Hassock marker for map visibility and is not an exact historic meadow coordinate.
